claims.text: Nearly 1,000 arrests were made across France as hundreds of thousands protested on Saturday, according to French officials.
The French interior ministry estimated that 410,000 people protested on Saturday, while trade unions reported about 800,000 participants.
French authorities deployed 70,000 police officers across several cities to manage protests over the cost of living and school conditions.
French President Emmanuel Macron decreed that only demonstrations organised by recognised trade unions would be permitted.
French Interior Minister Laurent Nuñez stated that two people were seriously injured during Saturday's protests, in Toulouse and Clermont-Ferrand.
Riot police in Tirana, Albania, fired tear gas to disperse thousands of anti-government demonstrators on Saturday.
Around 550,000 people participated in demonstrations across France the previous weekend, resulting in more than 2,500 arrests.
French authorities imposed partial curfews in certain urban zones of Paris and other cities.
Major Paris museums, including the Louvre and the Musée d'Orsay, closed on Saturday ahead of scheduled protests.
The main Paris protest march drew between 110,000 and 250,000 attendees according to authority and trade union estimates.
Interior Minister Laurent Nuñez reported a 20-year-old man had his fingers blown off in Toulouse during the protests.
Italian police arrested nine people and briefly detained 371 others across eight cities during protests on Saturday.
Italian police stated that 110 of the people arrested or detained during protests in Italy were minors.
The Italian government deployed 500 soldiers to Milan following looting during protests the previous weekend.
Ukraine announced on Saturday that the Starlink satellite system and Starshield military system were restored to pre-restriction operating speeds.
SpaceX CEO Elon Musk stated on X that Ukraine's military violated Starlink terms of service by using it for offensive drone strikes.
Ukrainian presidential adviser Serhiy Beskrestnov stated Ukraine is physically unable to use Starlink for long and medium range attack drone operations.
Ukrainian officials said previous Starshield speed caps of 160 kph hampered interception of Russian drones.
Ukraine's defence ministry stated Starlink connectivity remained stable at speeds over 400 kph on Saturday.
US Secretary of State Marco Rubio stated US President Donald Trump has no role in decisions made by Starlink and Starshield.
US President Donald Trump announced a deal to buy Russian diesel while urging Kyiv to stop striking Russian oil refineries.
The Biden and Trump administrations repeatedly requested SpaceX to activate or restrict Starlink in various countries, according to a Reuters report.
Russia agreed to resume three-way negotiations with Washington and Kyiv next month following a US diplomatic initiative.
Moscow and Kyiv agreed to a localized ceasefire around Oleshky, brokered by US First Lady Melania Trump.
Ukraine's defense ministry reported Starlink and Starshield operating speeds were stable at more than 250 mph on Saturday.
Restrictions had previously capped Starlink operating speeds in Ukraine at about 100 mph.
Ukrainian forces attacked a chemical plant in the Russian city of Tolyatti on Saturday.
A Russian drone struck a residential building in Kyiv's Obolon District on Saturday, causing a fire.
Two Israeli soldiers were killed in a shooting attack near Hebron on Friday morning.
Israel initiated a sweeping military operation and lockdown across the occupied West Bank following the Hebron attack.
Hebron Mayor Youssef al-Jaabari stated more than 1,000 people were displaced by Israeli demolitions in the Ein Deir Baha and Farsh al-Hawa neighbourhoods.
Two Palestinian gunmen killed two Israeli soldiers and injured three others at a checkpoint near Hebron before being killed.
Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu announced he reviewed plans for the largest military operation in the West Bank since 1967.
Israeli Finance Minister Bezalel Smotrich called for a comprehensive military campaign in the West Bank similar to operations in Gaza and Lebanon.
The Hebron municipality estimated 35 hectares (86 acres) were destroyed or marked for destruction in the district of Ein Deir Baha.
Israeli Finance Minister Bezalel Smotrich filmed himself wearing body armour in front of a Palestinian building being demolished in Hebron.
Hebron Mayor Yousef al-Ja'bari stated 2,200 people were forced from their homes by Israeli forces in Hebron.
Israeli Defence Minister Israel Katz confirmed about 2,000 people were displaced in Hebron.
Israeli forces fired a stun grenade at Al Jazeera journalists near the Farsh al-Hawa checkpoint in Hebron.
Israeli forces arrested about 70 Palestinians during raids across at least 15 areas of the West Bank, according to the Palestinian Prisoners' Society.
Nine people were killed when gunmen opened fire at a funeral at St George's Greek Orthodox church in Hamoud, Jordan.
Jordan's health minister reported 40 people were injured in the shooting at St George's Greek Orthodox church.
Security camera footage showed three attackers firing at the church entrance while taking cover behind trees and a low wall.
Jordanian Prime Minister Jafar Hassan stated on X that the church attack was the result of a terrorist ideology and blind extremism.
King Abdullah II visited Karak following the attack and promised the perpetrators would be punished with an iron fist.
St George's Greek Orthodox church is located in Karak, about 90 kilometers south of Jordan's capital, Amman.
Jordan declared three days of national mourning following the church attack in Karak.
Reuters updated the death toll from the church shooting in Karak, Jordan, to eight people killed.
Indian External Affairs Minister S Jaishankar condemned the church attack in Jordan and expressed solidarity with the Jordanian government and people.
Senator Flávio Bolsonaro defeated incumbent President Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva in the first round of Brazil's presidential election on October 4.
Flávio Bolsonaro is the son of imprisoned former Brazilian president Jair Bolsonaro.
President Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva addressed supporters at Copacabana Beach in Rio de Janeiro on the final day of campaigning.
Flávio Bolsonaro received 47 percent of the vote in the first round of Brazil's election, compared to Lula's 45 percent.
A CNT/MDA survey released on Saturday showed Flávio Bolsonaro leading with 46.3 percent against Lula's 45 percent.
Former Brazilian President Jair Bolsonaro is serving a 27-year prison sentence for attempting a coup after losing the 2022 election.
Nearly 159 million Brazilians are eligible to vote in the presidential election run-off on Sunday.
Rio's City Hall estimated that about 1.1 million people attended Lula's campaign rally at Copacabana beach.
Lula attended a large campaign rally on Paulista Avenue in São Paulo on Saturday afternoon.
Flávio Bolsonaro stated at campaign rallies that he will join Donald Trump's Shield of the Americas regional security initiative if elected.
